Clearstone Engineering Ltd. (2004). A National Inventory of Greenhouse Gas (GHG), Criteria Air Contaminant (CAC) and Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S) Emissions by the Upstream Oil and Gas Industry, Volume 5: Compendium of Terminology, Information Sources, Emission Factors, Equipment Schedules and Uncertainty Data. Prepared for the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers (CAPP), Calgary, September 2004.

Loaded (main): fugitive factors for the device-type sources in Tables 3.1/3.2 (fuel-gas service controllers, chemical injection pumps, compressor seals; gas vs oil facilities) as kg THC/h per source (THC not CH4, written under target ch4 - apply speciation); generic CH4 and N2O combustion factors from Table 3.3 (ng/J fuel input, HHV) for natural-gas reciprocating engines (2SLB, 4SLB, 4SRB), gas turbines, diesel engines, the flare factor and the <29 MW heater. Not loaded: ~300 engine-model-specific factor sets (Caterpillar, Waukesha, etc.) in Table 3.3, CAC pollutants (NOx, CO, PM, VOC, SO2), other component types (connectors, valves, OELs - baseline fugitives, no archetype), equipment schedules (Table 4.1-4.5, component and controller counts per facility type - inventory inputs), information sources (Sect. 2), uncertainty tables (Sect. 5). No glycol dehydrator emission factors in this volume (terminology only) and no costs or energy use. Uncertainty fractions kept in notes; their convention is ambiguous (p.50 example multiplies EF by lower/upper fractions) so no min/max derived. References are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 4). Most combustion factors are reprinted from US EPA AP-42.
